messages.subject: y_pred data and Parameter Recovery
parts:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am a PhD student who intends to use hBayesDM's bart_par4 model for 2 of my studies.

As someone with not much knowledge of programming, your package has been very user-friendly and helps me successfully conducting the parameter estimation for my data, and I am truly thankful to have come across your R package.

I would be much appreciated if you could help me further for the steps post-parameter estimation - the parameter recovery.
I obtained a y_pred (trial-level posterior predictive simulations) in my model output, however, I am not sure about the following points:

1.  Can y_pred be used for parameter recovery?
If not, how could I simulate data for this model? 

2. The outputted y_pred data was a 4-dimensions array:
8,000(iterations) * 102(subject)*30(trials)*125(max.pumps)
with 3 types of value : "1", "0", "NA".
I have then taken the last iteration out (it becomes 3D) then convert it into a 2D matrix -> 102*30, 125,
the resulting y_pred2D data has 3060 rows, 125 columns, all are 1,0,or NA. 

Does each row represent 1 Subject*1 Trial and each column represents whether the subject pump (=1) or not pump(cashed-in=0) for that Nth pump, and NA represents a burst? 

I thought so but for some trials (rows) the data is e.g. 1 0 0 1 0 1 NA NA NA...so I am confused about the meanings of the 1 and 0 in the y_pred data.

Yours sincerely,
Crystal

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: y_pred data and Parameter Recovery
parts:
Hi Crystal, 

Thanks for your good words about the package!
1. Can y_pred be used for parameter recovery?

--> No. You would need to program your own code for generating simulated data. I'm sorry that we don't provide a template or an example code for that yet..

2. I believe 1, 0, and NA indicate pump, not pump, and not available (because either the balloon exploded or the participant cashed out prior to that trial).

For posterior predictive check for a single subject, I would average the 4D matrix across (8000) iterations and select the subject (e.g., the first subject), which will lead to 2D matrix (= 30 trials x max 125 pumps). Then you can compare actual choices and predictions from the model like here: https://ccs-lab.github.io/hBayesDM/articles/getting_started.html#posterior-predictive-checks. Make sure NA values will be removed when averaging 8000 or multiple iterations by using na.rm=TRUE in R. 

Best,
Young
